life_event: Born in 1937 as Mary Linda Patricia Vann in Wilmington, North Carolina. All indulgences filled by grandmother “Mama” and her stepfather Colonel Clifford N/A Childhood Radcliffe.
Pat’s brother Kent is born.

Pat’s mother, Margureitte, marries Lt. Clifford Radcliffe in Fort Bragg, NC. Childhood Patricia constantly berated her stepbrother, Kent, since his birth. Would throw temper tantrums until she got what she wanted. If she didn’t get what Childhood she wanted, she would manipulate her way towards her goal.
Dropped out of school, pregnant. Married SGT Gilbert “Junior” Taylor in Atlanta, Georgia. She had three children with
Gil, Susan, Debbie and Ronnie.
Daughter Susan is born
Daughter Debbie is born
Pat, Gil, Susan, and Debbie move to the Philippines where Gil is stationed.
Pat and the family move to North Carolina
Son Ronnie is born.
Pat and the family move to Falls Church, Virginia.
Pat and the family move to Germany.
Pat and family move to Fort Bragg, North Carolina
Pat’s brother Kent commits suicide. Pat’s daughter, Susan, marries Captain Bill Alford. During the wedding reception Pat
announced that she was going to divorce Gil. She also stated that she had a restraining order on him. The divorce went through soon after the announcement.
Pat suffered from pulmonary emboli (blood clots in the lungs) and was hospitalized. Met Tom Allanson. His parents, Walter & Carolyn Allanson, disapproved of divorce
and refused to accept Pat as a new woman in Tom’s life.
A family feud started with Tom’s parents and threats were made from both sides.
Pat and Tom moved to Zebulon, Georgia. Pat Radcliffe and Tom Allanson got married in a show tent at Morgan Horse Show in
Stone Mountain, Georgia. The wedding was exactly what she wanted as she dressed as her idol, Scarlett O’Hara. Tom and Pat purchase a farm in Zebulon, Georgia. They began their dream of raising

and showing horses on their farm, Kentwood Morgan Farm. Tom’s father, Walter, tries to push Tom out of his life. As a result, Pat takes the opportunity to file a sexual harassment complaint against Walter. This caused Tom to Spring 37 file a restraining order against Walter. The feud grew further when Walter believed 1974 Tom had stolen a rifle and pistol from his home. Tom and Pat’s house was searched but no firearms were found. Tom’s parents, Walter and Carolyn, were shot at while driving to Lake Lanier,
Georgia. Walter accused Tom of firing the shots. Tom kills his parents in his parent’s home. He is arrested soon after. Both Pat and
Tom give false alibis to the police and Tom is sentenced to life in prison.
Pat convinces Tom into a suicide pact. Pat befriends Tom’s grandparents and is put in their will instead of their own
daughter. Pat begins to poison Tom’s grandparents with arsenic. Her house and barns burned
down, presumably by her own hand, and forged Tom’s signature for the insurance checks. Pat Allanson arrested for the attempted murders of Paw and Nona Allanson (Tom’s
grandparents)
Pat’s attempted murder trial begins.
Jury finds Pat guilty of attempted murder. Judge Holt sentences Pat to two 10-year prison sentences, to be served consecutively.
She is sent to Hardwick Correctional Institute in Milledgeville, GA. Pat is released from prison. She now goes by the name of Pat Taylor. She joins up

with her daughter Debbie, a registered nurse, and pretended to be a registered nurse. Among the clients was the Crist family. Jimmy Crist, Sr. dies around the Christmas holidays. The family suspects that Pat may
not have been properly taking care of Jimmy and may have been poisoning his wife Betty. Fulton County Grand Jury indicts Pat and her daughter Debbie on seven counts for
their crimes against the Crist family including aggravated assault with intent to murder, theft, and impersonating a registered nurse.
Pat reaches a plea agreement and is sentenced to 8 years in prison. Pat once again is released from jail. She opens up a shop in GA and lives with her
stepfather. Pat has a small, local doll shop called Pat’s Pretty Playthings.

Pat’s son Ronnie passes away. Pat is arrested again for doctor shopping, she may have received more than 3,700 pain February 70 pills in the past year. Her bail was set at $22,500 for three felony counts of 2008 unauthorized distribution.
